items.title: Qiyām bi-Nafsihi
items.summary:
It is an attribute of the Islamic God Allah. It roughly means “self-subsistence” or “self-existence.” It is a fundamental attribute that makes God Al-Qayyūm. The implications of this attribute can be surmised as so.
God is entirely independent of everything. Everything entirely is dependent on God. That is, God sustains himself, and the Creations. These statements imply a favourable conclusion. Let us look at the following arguments.
Everything is created by God. By (1), (2), and (3), God and the Creations cannot share any similarities at all. By (4), God is transcendent, and therefore, not immanent. By (5), the essence of God cannot be ever conceived with worldly logics. For (4): the argument arises from the consequence that if is God is self-subsistent, then everything about God is self-subsistent. Therefore, the Creations cannot have a part of God, which, if not held, will mean that the Creations is not entirely dependent on God, that some of the Creations are self-subsistent. However the following arguments pose a contradiction.

items.title: Somewhere’s My God
items.summary:
So tell me my dear so-called God, Why do you create sin and punish me for it?
Tell me why do you create so beautiful These things that sting me when I touch it?
You give me this voice that you never hear And a depth of heart that drowns me.
Why do you throw me into this abrupt existence, With no foreboding, no warning, nor admonition?
They speak that in you I find peace, and there seems Never anything more peaceful than never being born at all.
